clue.text: Problem when running a streaker can do without

definitions.meaning: a sharp pain in the side that runners often suffer
a streaker runs naked, without a single thread of clothing on

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on the phrase 'not a stitch on': the naked runner wears nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner's side pain and the smallest scrap of clothing share one word, so this double definition works through two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Suitable performance to Water Music?

parts.note: water from a tap suggests a dance done to tap water, a joke on Handel's Water Music

explanation.definitionFit: A dance with metal-tipped shoes, punningly fitted to music about water from a tap.

clue.text: Reptile's quiet, buried in the ground

indicators.note: buried in puts the quiet letter inside the word for ground

parts.note: terrain is ground or land
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

explanation.surface: A reptile lies silently buried in the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater turtle is a reptile.

clue.text: Cheer up! Welsh chap's upset a new boy at school

indicators.note: up in a down clue tells us the cheer is read from bottom to top

parts.note: rah is a cheer

indicators.note: upset tells us the Welsh name is turned upside down in this down clue

parts.note: Ivor is a typical Welsh man's name

explanation.surface: A Welshman is upset by a new boy at school and is told to cheer up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RAH into HAR and 'upset' turns IVOR into ROVI. HARROW is an English public school; its pupils are known by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil of Harrow School, an English public school, is known by this name.

clue.text: Boy who's big in New York, possibly?

definitions.meaning: New York is the Big Apple, and this is a variety of apple first grown in New York State

explanation.walkthrough: 'Big' suggests a famous person, but it hints at the Big Apple, New York's nickname; the answer is also an apple variety from that state.
explanation.definitionFit: A common male first name that is also an apple variety, the apple linking to the city's nickname.

clue.text: Labour's reward, after patient type took seat, is discord

parts.note: Job, of the Bible, is the model of patience
sat means took a seat
faction means internal dissent or strife

explanation.surface: Someone sat in a waiting room as a patient, finding party conflict the reward of the Labour party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' looks medical but refers to Job, the biblical figure of endurance. 'after' only orders the clue's own reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The contentment gained from doing one's work well is the reward of labour.

clue.text: Fruit unequally divided by one famous liar

indicators.note: divided by puts the numeral into the fruit, splitting it unequally

parts.note: ananas is another word for pineapple
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A fruit is cut unevenly by a notorious liar.
explanation.walkthrough: The I goes after ANAN, splitting the fruit into unequal parts. Ananias in Acts lied about money and was struck dead.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Acts, Ananias lied to the apostles and became a byword for a liar.

clue.text: No opera house at first in capital of state

indicators.note: at first tells us the letters for house go at the front

parts.note: taken as written
Lulu is Alban Berg's opera

explanation.surface: There is no opera house at first in a state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' moves HO to the front of NO + LULU.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of the US state of Hawaii.

clue.text: Paragon unchosen, oddly

indicators.note: oddly tells us the letters of unchosen are arranged in a strange order

explanation.surface: A model of excellence was strangely passed over.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a person or thing without equal, a model of perfection.

clue.text: Cut that was given to first mate

definitions.text: Cut that was given to first mate

parts.words: Cut that was given to first mate
parts.note: a cut of pork, read as the extra bone from Adam's side that Genesis says God used to make Eve, the first wife

explanation.definitionFit: A cut of pork ribs, read as the bone Adam could spare, from which Eve, his mate, was formed.

clue.text: Gun shot, hitting more than one target

definitions.text: shot, hitting more than one target
definitions.meaning: in billiards, a stroke in which the cue ball strikes two other balls in turn

explanation.walkthrough: 'Gun shot' reads as one phrase but splits into two definitions; the second is the billiards stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: An artillery piece and a billiards stroke striking two balls share one spelling.

clue.text: Womaniser caught when a star appears

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'
a nova is a star that suddenly flares in brightness

explanation.surface: A ladies' man is caught out just as a celebrity turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after the eighteenth-century Venetian adventurer famous for his seductions, the name means a serial seducer.

clue.text: Comic actor divided parts of the country

definitions.meaning: W. C. ..., the American film comedian
enclosed areas of farmland in the countryside, split off by hedges or fences

explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' here means countryside, not a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the comedian W. C. Fields is also the word for parcels of farmland.

clue.text: First and second signs in abbreviated form

definitions.text: First and second signs in abbreviated form

parts.words: First and second signs in abbreviated form
parts.note: a person who signs with only the first letters of the first and second names signs in shortened form

explanation.definitionFit: Signing a document with just the first letters of one's names is signing in abbreviated form.

clue.text: Let out learner I told off

parts.note: L is the learner-driver plate
berated means scolded

explanation.surface: A learner driver is released after being scolded.
explanation.definitionFit: Freed or released, as a prisoner who is let out of jail.

clue.text: Axed when moving West

indicators.note: moving tells us the letter for West is shifted to another place in the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tree was felled while the woodsman was heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' shifts the W of WHEN from the front to third place.
explanation.definitionFit: Hewn is the past participle of hew, to chop with an axe, so it means cut down with an axe.

clue.text: What you could get with shot badly executed?

definitions.text: What you could get with shot badly executed?

indicators.note: badly executed tells us the letters of what and shot are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cricketer plays a poor stroke and hears the bowler's appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly executed' rearranges WHATSHOT. In cricket, 'How's that?' (howzat) is the fielders' appeal to the umpire for a dismissal, likely after a poor shot.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket appeal to the umpire for a dismissal, the likely result of a poorly played stroke.

clue.text: Catholic writer about love is vulnerable to attack

parts.note: catholic with a small c means broad or wide-ranging
love is zero in tennis, O
a pen is a writing tool

explanation.surface: A Catholic author writing about love leaves himself open to criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catholic' looks religious, but read as catholic it means broad.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposed and undefended, as a goal left unguarded.

clue.text: Indication of pain that makes one buckle

definitions.meaning: an old word for a clasp or brooch that fastens clothing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Buckle' looks like collapsing in pain, but here it means to fasten: the word is also an archaic name for a clasp.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry of hurt is also an archaic noun for a jewelled clasp, something that fastens a garment.

clue.text: Bully, one who's soft? That's a contradiction in terms

parts.note: bully as an adjective means like a bull, ox-like, so oxy
a moron is someone soft in the head

explanation.surface: Calling a bully soft is self-contradictory.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek roots mean sharp-dull, itself a contradiction.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure of speech pairing opposites, like 'deafening silence', contradicts itself.

clue.text: Coping, partly, with gangster getting in the way

indicators.note: getting in puts the street inside the gangster's name

parts.note: Al Capone, the Chicago gangster
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Dealing with a gangster who gets in the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coping' looks like managing, but it is the top course of a wall; the answer is part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Coping is the top course of a wall; each stone in it is one piece of that course.

clue.text: Put out wood to make tobacco container

parts.note: to snuff a candle is to put it out
box is a tree whose hard timber is called boxwood

explanation.surface: Someone extinguishes a fire built of timber to produce a little case for tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: A small lidded case holding powdered tobacco for sniffing.

clue.text: Dignified country lady taking no notice

parts.note: a state is a country

indicators.note: taking no tells us the notice is removed from the word lady

parts.note: taken as written
an ad is a notice in a paper

explanation.surface: A dignified noblewoman of the land pays no attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking no' removes AD from LADY, leaving LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand and majestic in manner, impressive and solemn.

clue.text: Oscillate with ease, changing between two directions

indicators.note: between puts the rearranged letters inside the pair of compass points

parts.note: S and W are the compass points south and west

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of ease are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something swings comfortably back and forth between two compass bearings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two directions' gives a pair of compass points, which the solver must choose: south and west fit, with the rearranged letters set between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To move up and down or back and forth, like a plank on a pivot, is to swing to and fro.

clue.text: Expert at the wheel, perhaps, smashing car times

indicators.note: smashing tells us the letters of car and times are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A driver, an expert at the wheel, keeps crashing the car repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expert at the wheel' suggests a driver, but it is a potter's wheel. 'smashing' rearranges CARTIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: A potter making pottery at the wheel is one example of a maker of ceramics; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Device for feeding insect

definitions.meaning: a funnel-shaped container that feeds grain or material into a machine
a grasshopper or similar jumping insect

explanation.definitionFit: A funnel feeding a machine and a jumping insect such as a grasshopper share the name.

clue.text: For winter coming, install this telephone system in part of house

indicators.note: install this tells us to put the answer inside part of a house, and the result spells out the phrase winter coming

explanation.surface: Ahead of winter, someone fits a phone system in a room of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: Put the answer inside WING, part of a house, and you get W-INTERCOM-ING, 'winter coming'.
explanation.definitionFit: An internal phone or speaker network linking rooms of a building.

clue.text: Poet's composed sonnet about city

indicators.note: about puts the rearranged letters around the city
composed tells us the letters of sonnet are arranged afresh

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York City

explanation.surface: A poet has written a sonnet about a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' turns SONNET into TENSON, which goes 'about' NY.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was a Victorian Poet Laureate.

clue.text: He won't admit it's a unit of weight

definitions.meaning: a unit measuring the fineness of yarn, as in stockings described by their weight per length

explanation.walkthrough: The unit is used for nylon and silk thread: the mass in grams of 9,000 metres of yarn.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who denies, and a measure of thread fineness, share a spelling.
